movers.reason: The flip window is open and the edge has not decayed — if anything it has widened on a sample three times larger than when it was first measured. Rising players still rise at the next tick the large majority of the time, and the board still pays exactly market value on the way out, so a bid placed at market value on a rising board listing is a free option: win it and the tick is captured, lose it and it cost nothing. Never raise. The important finding this run is that the book is bigger than it looks, because the legs do not overlap in time. Four of them expire before tonight's tick and one expires after it, so summing the outlays overstates the exposure badly and would wrongly rule the largest leg out. Sequenced properly the whole book clears with room to spare and lands positive at the lock. There is exactly one way to get it wrong, and it is not price: if the pre-tick legs are still held when the late one settles, the floor breaks and there is no recovery inside the matchday. Sell the pre-tick legs back as soon as tonight's tick has run, before the late leg lands, or skip the late leg entirely. Two open questions stand unresolved: whether Kickbase caps squad size, which would cap how many flips can be in flight at once; and that this edge is measured in one league over one period and will decay if the rivals here crowd into it — the four most active traders in this league were last season's top four finishers, and they flip the tick constantly, injured players included, which for a pure value flip is correct.
